decisive_items: central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism
response.rationale: Erdheim-Chester disease is a non-Langerhans histiocytosis with CD68-positive, CD1a/S-100-negative infiltrates, foam cells, and systemic involvement including central diabetes insipidus; the skin findings and endocrine history align strongly. Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma shares granulomatous infiltrate but lacks the endocrine pattern and typically has periorbital involvement with paraproteinemia.

rejected.why: CD1a and S-100 negative contradict Langerhans cell histiocytosis
Same CD1a/S-100 negativity excludes Langerhans cell histiocytosis
Foam cells present but no systemic endocrine pattern; Niemann-Pick usually has neurologic/hepatic features
MEN1 does not explain skin histiocytic infiltrate or CD68 positivity
Gaucher disease typically has glucocerebrosidase deficiency and organomegaly, not this skin/IHC profile
